learningObjective: Explain how tensor parallelism shards MLP and attention weights across devices and what collective is required per layer.

canonicalClaims.claim: Megatron-style TP shards W_up column-wise and W_down row-wise (analogously for attention QKV / output projection); one AllReduce per MLP (and one per attention) sums partial outputs across TP ranks.
conditions: Input x is replicated across TP ranks entering each transformer block.
nonImplications: Does not imply TP is always the best strategy.

misconceptions.claim: TP requires AllGather of the intermediate before W_down.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The row-column arrangement is designed to avoid AllGather; a single AllReduce at the end suffices.

misconceptions.claim: TP works with zero communication because sharding aligns perfectly.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Partial products from each rank must be summed via AllReduce.

misconceptions.claim: Only one of W_up or W_down is sharded in TP.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both are sharded to save memory; the point is column-then-row.

implementationFacts: Attention analog: QKV projection column-parallel, output projection row-parallel, one AllReduce per attention block.
SwiGLU with fused gate/up: both gate and up are column-parallel; down is row-parallel.
performanceScenarios: TP scales best on NVLink-connected GPUs; scaling across nodes over InfiniBand is more limited.
AllReduce bandwidth is often the bottleneck for very large TP degrees.
